key_insight: The paper shows that Rust’s ownership model can be leveraged with Aeneas and Lean to verify real cryptographic production code at scale, with AI agents helping generate proofs that Lean independently checks.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to verify high-performance cryptographic libraries without rewriting them in a verification-friendly language, while preserving deployment, portability, and performance goals.
method: Extract Rust code into a pure Lean model using Aeneas
Use Lean tactics and libraries to prove safety, panic-freedom, and functional correctness
Employ AI agents to draft proofs and formalize standards/intrinsics under expert review
evidence_signal: The authors report a 237 KLOC Lean development verifying 16.7 KLOC of Rust code for post-quantum cipher suites across x86-64 and ARM platforms.
watch_item: The approach still depends on expert design and review for cryptographic standards and platform-specific intrinsics, which may remain a bottleneck.
paper_title: Scaling Verification of Cryptographic Software with Aeneas, Rust, and Lean
